title: Nonlinear Geometrizability of State-Dependent Proto-Area in Approximate Holographic Codes
abstract: State-dependent proto-area data produced by approximate recovery need not be compatible with a single local bulk metric. Using recovery maps calibrated on the code channel and held fixed along a logical-state family, we derive exact finite-resolution criteria and, near the hyperbolic disk, necessary and sufficient conditions for a regular proto-area two-jet to arise from a metric two-jet on a time-reflection-symmetric asymptotically AdS$_3$ slice. Finite networks give a polyhedral realization problem with primal and dual certificates, stable reconstruction, and explicit witnesses of nongeometry. In the continuum, the geometric tangent space is the range of the rank-two geodesic X-ray transform. A metric-forced Jacobi equation determines the normal Hessian of the renormalized boundary-length image and yields a gauge-invariant quadratic obstruction. Under a split-regularity hypothesis, nearby geometric data form a local graph; the two-jet criterion itself is unconditional for regular data. Hamiltonian-skewed codes realize both first-order nongeometry and a response whose first obstruction appears only at quadratic order. The compatible metric perturbation is reconstructed modulo boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms.
summary: This work rigorously investigates when state-dependent entropy measurements, arising in the context of holographic quantum error correction, correspond to actual local bulk geometries. It establishes a hierarchy of necessary and sufficient conditions—requiring matching first and second-order differential constraints—to prove this geometric compatibility. This bridges advanced topics in quantum information theory with differential geometry.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the nonlinear geometrizability of state-dependent proto-area data derived from approximate holographic recovery processes.
main_result: Geometrizability requires satisfying both first-order (linear) and second-order (quadratic) consistency conditions, which are necessary and sufficient for local metric reconstruction under regularity assumptions.
method: The analysis employs tools from differential geometry, including the geodesic X-ray transform, Jacobi equations, and jet calculus to establish rigorous mathematical criteria for geometric realization.
model_or_system: The framework is set in the context of AdS/CFT holography applied to quantum error correction codes. The input data is the state-dependent proto-area ($	ext{SPA}$), which measures entropy differences related to boundary regions.
key_observables: Proto-Area Map ($	ext{SPA}$), first and second order obstructions ($\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}a_1}$, $\mathcal{O}_2$), and the reconstructed metric two-jet $(h_1, h_2)$.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the regularity of the logical state family ($\Sigma$) and the approximation level (finite network vs. continuum).
main_assumptions: Assumptions include 'recovery-regularity' for the state manifold and the applicability of split-regularity hypotheses to ensure smooth local geometric structures.
figures_summary: Figures summarize geometrizability criteria across different levels (network, first jet, two-jet) and compare various bounds on reconstruction errors.
paper_structure: The paper develops from finite network realization problems using linear algebra constraints to the continuum limit, establishing necessary conditions via Jacobi equations for the second jet, and concluding with explicit reconstruction formulas modulo boundary diffeomorphisms.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework connecting quantum information measures (entropy/area) derived from holographic codes directly to fundamental geometric properties of spacetime metrics in AdS space.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Geometrizability as a common-source condition. A fixed code and recovery prescription produce a proto-area map from logical states to interval data. Local metrics generate only the nonlinear locus GgH = Im B. Data on this locus reconstruct a metric modulo boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms. Tangential or normal components incompatible with the locus yield boundary- accessible nongeometric witnesses.

Figure 2. Fixed four-terminal geometry and local consistency relations. (a) Background weights from Equation (3.64). (b,c) The heavy edges are the selected cuts for regions 12 and 23, which imply q12 = q1 + q2 and q23 = q2 + q3. Violating either identity rules out a local edge-weight realization in this chamber.

Figure 3. Linear geometrizability on the hyperbolic disk. (a) Every boundary interval probes the same local metric perturbation along its reference geodesic. (b) The scalar and rank-two transverse-traceless sectors form the closed geometric range in the source-adapted data topology; sectors of order four and above are nongeometric for a metric perturbation. (c) A finite calculation measures a rectangular set of moment witnesses. Enlarging the window converges monotonically to the exact nongeometric defect.

Figure 4. The nonlinear geometric data locus near the hyperbolic background. Its tangent space is the rank-two X-ray range Ygeo. A genuine metric path has normal acceleration fixed by the second fundamental form IIgH. A proto-area path can share the same first derivative while differing by a quadratic obstruction O2, which no second-order metric coefficient can remove.

Figure 5. Controlled bond skews. Local Schmidt rotations alter the entropy of each crossed bond independently and produce data in Im MC. A cross-cell gate between separated bond modes produces a connected cut response b×. The susceptibility χ(r) in (6.27) is strictly positive away from the maximally entangled point.
